headline_marked: 74 families of [[victims of democratic movements get jobs]] from PM
headline: 74 families of victims of democratic movements get jobs from PM
summary: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman handed over appointment letters to families of those killed or injured in the July Uprising and victims of enforced disappearances.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman handed over job appointment letters to 74 individuals, including family members of those killed or injured during the July Uprising and victims of enforced disappearances.

Speaking at the Prime Minister's Office in Tejgaon, the PM pledged that the government is committed to fulfilling the aspirations of those who sacrificed their lives for independence, democracy, and people's rights.
He emphasized that the government would not retreat from this path despite practical difficulties and limitations in meeting all expectations within the desired timeframe.
The PM stated that the support provided to affected families is not mere assistance, but a reflection of the government's commitment to the aspirations of the martyrs.
He noted that the 20 crore people of Bangladesh have been freed from a fascist situation through the sacrifices of those who are no longer present.
The Prime Minister also prayed for those who remain missing and urged the families to continue supporting the government in its efforts to restore democracy.
Recipients included family members of victims of enforced disappearance and killing, as well as visually impaired fighters from the July Uprising.
The event was attended by Cabinet Secretary Nasimul Gani, the PM's Principal Secretary, and other high-ranking officials.
caption:
74 family members of martyrs and victims of enforced disappearances have been given government jobs.

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman handed over job appointment letters to 74 individuals, including family members of those killed or injured during the July Uprising and victims of enforced disappearances.

Speaking at the Prime Minister's Office in Tejgaon, the PM pledged that the government is committed to fulfilling the aspirations of those who sacrificed their lives for independence, democracy, and people's rights.

He emphasized that the government would not retreat from this path despite practical difficulties and limitations in meeting all expectations within the desired timeframe.

The PM stated that the support provided to affected families is not mere assistance, but a reflection of the government's commitment to the aspirations of the martyrs.

He noted that the 20 crore people of Bangladesh have been freed from a fascist situation through the sacrifices of those who are no longer present.

The Prime Minister also prayed for those who remain missing and urged the families to continue supporting the government in its efforts to restore democracy.

Recipients included family members of victims of enforced disappearance and killing, as well as visually impaired fighters from the July Uprising.

The event was attended by Cabinet Secretary Nasimul Gani, the PM's Principal Secretary, and other high-ranking officials.

headline: Primary school headteacher dies after falling from rickshaw during mugging
summary: Ronjina Parvin, 55, suffered severe head injuries after two motorcycle-borne muggers tried to snatch her bag near the Jatiya Sangsad Bhaban in Dhaka.
details: A 55-year-old primary school teacher died after falling from a rickshaw when two muggers allegedly tried to snatch her bag in front of the Jatiya Sangsad Bhaban in Dhaka this morning.
The deceased was identified as Ronjina Parvin, headmistress of Bagbari Girls Government Primary School in Gabtali upazila of Bogura.
According to the Dhaka Metropolitan Police, Ronjina had traveled from Bogura with her husband to consult a doctor at the Ispahani Islamia Eye Institute and Hospital at Farmgate.
Around 6:30 am, as their rickshaw reached the South Plaza area of the parliament complex, two muggers on a motorcycle approached from behind and attempted to snatch her bag.
During the scuffle, Ronjina fell from the rickshaw and sustained severe head injuries.
She was rushed to Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College Hospital, where doctors declared her dead.

Around 6:30 am, as their rickshaw reached the South Plaza area of the parliament complex, two muggers on a motorcycle approached from behind and attempted to snatch her bag.
